record.summary: Guidance under Article 33(3) of Korea's AI Basic Act, which lets the Minister of Science and ICT establish and disseminate guidelines on the criteria and examples of 'high-impact AI'. It sets a two-step test: whether the AI system is used in an area listed in Article 2(4), such as energy supply, drinking water, health care, medical devices, nuclear safety, analysis of biometric information for criminal investigation or arrest, hiring and loan screening, transport, public-service decisions or student assessment; and whether that use may significantly affect or endanger life, physical safety or fundamental rights. Area-by-area decision flows and examples follow.
record.notes: Published on 22 January 2026, when the Act entered into force. NIA records revised uploads on 29 January 2026 (decision flows for criminal investigation and arrest), 13 February 2026 (health-care criteria and a non-applicable example) and 29 April 2026 (health-care decision flow); the file recorded here is the 29 April 2026 version (216 pages). Operators judge for themselves whether their AI is high-impact and may ask the Minister to confirm; the guideline says it is not legally binding, that the expert committee's advice on a request is non-binding and optional, and that the Minister's confirmation is an administrative view on which the courts have the final say. Annexes reproduce the Act (Act No. 20676), the draft Enforcement Decree and the request forms. MSIT's online form for confirmation requests asks operators to review the guideline first and refers them to an advice desk.

verification.note: Stored: NIA's copy of the guideline (PDF, 216 pages, version of 29 April 2026; pages 1 to 6 have no text layer), MSIT's online form for high-impact AI confirmation requests (stored as the record's secondary source) and NIA's post of 22 January 2026 distributing the AI Basic Act guidelines. The guideline confirms the title (in its own FAQ), the Article 33(3) basis, the two-step test, the area table of Article 2(4), the examples, the confirmation procedure and its non-binding character. NIA's post confirms the publication date, the revisions of 29 January, 13 February and 29 April 2026 and the current file. The cover image shows the English title 'Guidelines for Determining High-Impact AI Systems' and the logos of MSIT and NIA, but has no text layer. A September 2025 draft mentioned in an earlier version of this record is in no file stored for this record and is no longer stated.

judgment.status_reasoning: NIA's post of 22 January 2026 says the current versions of the AI Basic Act guidelines have been published (현재본이 공개되었습니다) and lists this guideline as the file of 29 April 2026, after revised uploads on 29 January, 13 February and 29 April 2026. The stored guideline (216 pages) states that it is not legally binding (page 214), and MSIT's confirmation-request form tells operators to review it before filing a request. No stored file shows a withdrawal or replacement, so 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands, with date_last_updated 2026-04-29.
judgment.scope_reasoning: In scope without a scope note: ministry guidance on the risk classification of an AI-specific statute.

changes.summary: Corrected a mistranslation that widened the defined class: Article 2(4)(f), reproduced on page 20, is one area, the analysis and use of biometric information for criminal investigation or arrest, not separate 'biometric identification' and 'criminal investigation' areas. Completed the list of areas from the page 20 table (medical devices, transport, student assessment). Dropped 'weighing impact, severity, frequency and the domain's specifics', which are the factors the Minister weighs on a confirmation request (decree, page 9), not the guideline's own test. The self-assessment sentence moved to notes.
changes.notes: Removed the September 2025 draft, which no stored file supports. Added what the guideline says about its legal force, the expert committee and the confirmation (pages 10 and 214). Named the advice desk without the KOSA attribution, which the stored MSIT page does not make.
changes.verification: New note saying what each stored file confirms.

open_questions: title: the issuer's own English title on the cover is 'Guidelines for Determining High-Impact AI Systems', but the cover has no text layer, so it cannot be quoted. If textify ran OCR on page 1, the title could become the issuer's English title.
The guideline cites the confirmation procedure as decree Article 24 (page 9), while the annexed draft decree numbers it Article 25 (page 194); the inconsistency is in the source, not in the record.
